claims.text: ERC-8004 is titled "Trustless Agents" and is a Standards Track ERC.
ERC-8004 has status Draft, not Final.
ERC-8004 was created on 2025-08-13.
The ERC-8004 file was first merged into the ethereum/ERCs repository on 2025-08-18 (pull request 1170).
ERC-8004 moved from Draft to Review on 2025-10-08.
On 2026-01-13 an EIP editor commit changed the ERC-8004 status from Review back to Draft.
The 2026-01-13 commit also added a requires line listing EIP-155, EIP-712, EIP-721 and ERC-1271.
The last change to the ERC-8004 specification file before 2026-10-18 was a commit on 2026-01-25 titled "Updates from community feedback".
The ERC-8004 header lists four authors: Marco De Rossi, Davide Crapis, Jordan Ellis and Erik Reppel.
Erik Reppel was added as an ERC-8004 author in the 2025-10-08 commit that moved the standard to Review.

The contracts README describes ERC-8004 as a community effort coordinated by Marco De Rossi (MetaMask) and Davide Crapis (Ethereum Foundation), co-authored by Jordan Ellis (Google) and Erik Reppel (Coinbase).
The ERC-8004 project website is 8004.org and the contact address in the README is team@8004.org.

No foundation or association governing ERC-8004 was found in the contracts README, on 8004.org or in a web search on 2026-10-18; the text changes through pull requests in the ethereum/ERCs repository.
The ERC-8004 specification text is released under CC0.
The reference registry contracts carry the SPDX license identifier MIT, while the README license section says CC0.
The ERC-8004 discussion thread is on Ethereum Magicians, topic 25098.

ERC-8004 does not move money: the specification says payments are orthogonal to the protocol, and the registries have no function that takes or forwards payments; the only payable entry point is the owner-only upgradeToAndCall inherited from OpenZeppelin UUPS.
ERC-8004 defines three registries: an Identity Registry, a Reputation Registry and a Validation Registry.
The specification expects the registries to be deployed as singletons per chain, and an agent registered on one chain can operate on other chains.
The Identity Registry is based on ERC-721 with the URIStorage extension, so each agent is an NFT.
In ERC-8004 the ERC-721 tokenId is called agentId, which the registry assigns incrementally, and the tokenURI is called agentURI.
A global agent identifier combines agentRegistry, formatted as {namespace}:{chainId}:{identityRegistry}, with the agentId.
The namespace in agentRegistry is eip155 for EVM chains.
The deployed Identity Registry implementation assigns agentId 0 to the first agent, and ownerOf(0) resolves on Ethereum mainnet.
The Identity Registry ERC-721 token has the name AgentIdentity and the symbol AGENT.
The Identity Registry has three register overloads: register(), register(string agentURI) and register(string agentURI, MetadataEntry[] metadata).
A MetadataEntry struct has two fields: metadataKey (string) and metadataValue (bytes).
Registration emits one Transfer event, one MetadataSet event for agentWallet, one MetadataSet per extra metadata entry, and a Registered event.
The Registered event has the parameters agentId (indexed), agentURI and owner (indexed).
setAgentURI(agentId, newURI) updates the agent URI and emits URIUpdated(agentId, newURI, updatedBy).
The MetadataSet event has the parameters agentId (indexed), indexedMetadataKey (indexed string), metadataKey and metadataValue.
getMetadata(agentId, metadataKey) returns bytes and setMetadata(agentId, metadataKey, metadataValue) stores bytes.
Only the owner or an approved operator can call setAgentURI, setMetadata, setAgentWallet and unsetAgentWallet in the reference implementation.
The metadata key agentWallet is reserved and cannot be set through setMetadata or during register.
The specification describes agentWallet as the address where the agent receives payments, initially set to the owner address.
Changing agentWallet requires setAgentWallet(agentId, newWallet, deadline, signature) with an EIP-712 signature from an EOA or an ERC-1271 signature from a contract wallet.

The reference implementation verifies an EIP-712 signature by the new wallet over AgentWalletSet(uint256 agentId,address newWallet,address owner,uint256 deadline) under the domain ERC8004IdentityRegistry, version 1.
The reference implementation rejects a setAgentWallet deadline more than 5 minutes in the future.
setAgentWallet reverts with "bad wallet", "expired", "deadline too far" or "invalid wallet sig" in the reference implementation.
getAgentWallet(agentId) reads the wallet and unsetAgentWallet(agentId) clears it.
When an agent NFT is transferred, agentWallet is cleared and the new owner must verify a wallet again.
The Identity Registry has no burn or deregistration function in the reference implementation.
The agentURI must resolve to the agent registration file and may use any URI scheme, for example ipfs://, https:// or a base64 data: URI.
The registration file type value is https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1.
The registration file includes type, name, description, image, services, x402Support, active, registrations and supportedTrust.
Each services entry has a name and an endpoint, and version is recommended but not required.
The specification example lists service names web, A2A, MCP, OASF, ENS, DID and email.
Each registrations entry has agentId and agentRegistry, and all fields in a registration are mandatory.
supportedTrust is optional; example values are reputation, crypto-economic and tee-attestation, and if it is absent the ERC is used only for discovery.
An agent may prove control of an HTTPS endpoint domain by publishing https://{endpoint-domain}/.well-known/agent-registration.json with a matching registrations entry.

Neither the ERC-8004 text nor the ethereum/ERCs assets folder publishes a JSON Schema for the registration file, and the erc-8004 contracts and best-practices repositories hold none; the text gives the structure only as an example (checked 2026-10-18).
Feedback in the Reputation Registry is a signed fixed-point value (int128) with valueDecimals (uint8, 0 to 18).
The full feedback call is giveFeedback(agentId, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash).
giveFeedback requires agentId (a registered agent), value and valueDecimals; tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI and feedbackHash are optional.
The agent owner and approved operators must not give feedback to their own agent.
The reference implementation reverts self-feedback with the message "Self-feedback not allowed".
The Reputation Registry stores only value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2 and isRevoked for each feedback entry.
endpoint, feedbackURI and feedbackHash are emitted in the NewFeedback event but are not stored in contract storage.
feedbackIndex is a 1-indexed counter of feedback that a clientAddress has given to an agentId.
feedbackHash is the keccak256 hash of the content at feedbackURI and is optional for content-addressed URIs such as IPFS.
The NewFeedback event carries agentId, clientAddress, feedbackIndex, value, valueDecimals, indexedTag1, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI and feedbackHash.
A client can revoke its own feedback with revokeFeedback(agentId, feedbackIndex), which emits FeedbackRevoked.
Anyone can call appendResponse(agentId, clientAddress, feedbackIndex, responseURI, responseHash), which emits ResponseAppended.
Appended responses do not change the stored feedback value or the getSummary result in the reference implementation.
getSummary(agentId, clientAddresses, tag1, tag2) returns count, summaryValue and summaryValueDecimals.
getSummary requires a non-empty list of client addresses, and the reference implementation reverts with "clientAddresses required" otherwise.
The reference getSummary computes a plain mean of matching non-revoked values normalized to 18 decimals and reports it at the most common valueDecimals.
Other Reputation Registry reads are readFeedback, readAllFeedback, getResponseCount, getClients, getLastIndex and getIdentityRegistry.
The reference implementation limits the absolute feedback value to 1e38.
The specification gives example tag1 values starred, reachable, ownerVerified, uptime, successRate, responseTime, blocktimeFreshness, revenues and tradingYield.
In the specification example, an uptime of 99.77% is encoded as value 9977 with valueDecimals 2.
When the client is an agent, it should give feedback from its agentWallet address.
The off-chain feedback file must contain agentRegistry, agentId, clientAddress, createdAt, value and valueDecimals.
Optional feedback file fields include tag1, tag2, endpoint, mcp, a2a, oasf and proofOfPayment.
proofOfPayment in the feedback file has the fields fromAddress, toAddress, chainId and txHash.
proofOfPayment lives only in the off-chain feedback file; the registry stores no payment data and never verifies the proof.
The correct order is to publish the feedback file with proofOfPayment first and then call giveFeedback with its feedbackURI and feedbackHash.
The a2a object in the feedback file holds skills, contextId and taskId as defined by A2A.
The Validation Registry is specified with validationRequest(validatorAddress, agentId, requestURI, requestHash) and validationResponse(requestHash, response, responseURI, responseHash, tag).
validationRequest must be called by the owner or an operator of the agent, and only the named validator may call validationResponse.
A validation response is a value from 0 to 100 and may be submitted more than once, for example for soft and then hard finality.
Validator incentives and slashing are outside the scope of the Validation Registry.
The Validation Registry is not officially deployed: the contracts README lists no Validation Registry address on any chain.
The contracts README says the Validation Registry part of the spec is still under active update and discussion with the TEE community.
Testnet Validation Registry addresses were listed in the README from 2025-10-22 and dropped on 2026-01-06.
A contract at the scripted Validation address 0x8004Cc8439f36fd5F9F049D9fF86523Df6dAAB58 answered with version 2.0.0 on Ethereum and Base on 2026-10-11, but it is not listed or announced as deployed.
In the reference implementation a requestHash can be used only once ("exists"), so the first owner to submit a given hash occupies it.
Issue 28 reports that a validator can lower a response after a pass; a community fix in PR 51 was still unmerged on 2026-10-11.
The spec used endpoints and an agent-signed feedbackAuth in its Review version of 2025-10-08.
feedbackAuth was removed from the reference contracts on 2025-11-12 and from the specification on 2026-01-07; it no longer exists.
The 2026-01-07 spec update reserved agentWallet, added setAgentWallet and added x402Support and active to the registration file.
On 2026-01-25 the spec renamed endpoints to services and replaced score with value plus valueDecimals.
All three upgradeable registry implementations return version 2.0.0 from getVersion.
The Ethereum Mainnet Identity Registry is 0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432 and the Reputation Registry is 0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63.
Every mainnet in the README uses the same two registry addresses.
Testnets in the README use Identity 0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e and Reputation 0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713.
Ethereum Mainnet registry addresses were added to the contracts README on 2026-01-29.
Testnet deployments were first listed in the README on the default branch between 2025-10-22 and 2025-11-05, so testnets date from October to November 2025.
The contracts README lists 25 mainnets including Ethereum, that is 24 besides Ethereum.

On the default branch, fifteen mainnets were added to the contracts README in eight commits between 2026-02-02 and 2026-02-12, starting with Polygon, and five more (GOAT Network, Metis, SKALE Base, Soneium and XLayer) followed on 2026-03-06, for 21 in all.
Billions Mainnet was added to the README on 2026-04-08 and Injective Mainnet on 2026-04-09.
0G Mainnet was added to the README on 2026-06-11 and Robinhood Chain Mainnet on 2026-08-15.
README dates mark when a chain was listed, which can lag the on-chain deployment: the Soneium Identity proxy was created on 2026-02-12, 22 days before the README listed Soneium on 2026-03-06.
The registry proxies are deployed at the same addresses on each chain through CREATE2 and the Safe Singleton Factory at 0x914d7Fec6aaC8cd542e72Bca78B30650d45643d7.
All three registries are UUPS upgradeable proxies whose upgrade is restricted to the contract owner.
On Ethereum and Base the registry owner on 2026-10-11 was 0x547289319C3e6aedB179C0b8e8aF0B5ACd062603, an address with no contract code.

Who holds the registry owner key, the externally owned account 0x547289319C3e6aedB179C0b8e8aF0B5ACd062603, is not stated in the contracts repository or on 8004.org, and no announcement naming the holder was found (searched 2026-10-18).
New chains need the owner to authorize an upgrade from the MinimalUUPSMainnet placeholder to the registry implementations.
The specification states that Sybil attacks can inflate the reputation of fake agents and leaves mitigation to filtering by trusted reviewers.

The specification says ERC-8004 cryptographically ties the registration file to the on-chain agent but cannot cryptographically guarantee that advertised capabilities are functional and non-malicious; it leaves that check to its trust models (reputation, validation and TEE attestation).

Registration files served over HTTPS can change without any on-chain event; content-addressed URIs such as ipfs:// and on-chain data: URIs fix the content, so a change needs setAgentURI, which emits URIUpdated.
On 2026-10-18 the GitHub security advisory list of erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts was empty, and NVD keyword searches for ERC-8004 and erc-8004-contracts returned no CVE.
No audit report by a named audit firm is published in the erc-8004-contracts repository: none is on the default branch, and the community audit in PR 51 was still open and unmerged on 2026-10-18.
A community audit in PR 51 reported 1 high, 3 medium, 3 low and 2 informational findings.
ERC-8004 natively supports the reputation control through its Reputation Registry.
The ERC-8004 text and its reference contracts define no spending caps, consent capture, step-up authentication or kill switch.
Dispute support in ERC-8004 is limited to appended responses, such as an agent showing a refund.
The ERC-8004 text and the reference Identity Registry define no KYC or know-your-agent check; register is open to any address.
The specification says on-chain pointers and hashes cannot be deleted, which matters if personal data is placed in feedback.
The specification notes that applications can sponsor feedback gas using EIP-7702 because clients need not be registered.

On 2026-04-14 The Graph announced that its Agent0 subgraphs were live on Base, BNB Chain, Ethereum, Monad and Polygon; the post says they had already served millions of queries and gives no launch date.
The Agent0 subgraphs index the Registered, MetadataSet, NewFeedback, FeedbackRevoked, ValidationRequest and ValidationResponse events.
8004scan.io is an ERC-8004 explorer whose footer says it is powered by AltLayer.
agentscan.info is an ERC-8004 explorer published as "Agentscan by alias".
The npm package agent0-sdk was at version 1.7.1 on 2026-10-11, MIT licensed, from the agent0lab/agent0-ts repository.
The PyPI package agent0-sdk was at version 1.7.1 on 2026-10-11.
The npm package create-8004-agent was at version 1.4.2 on 2026-10-11.
ChaosChain publishes @chaoschain/sdk on npm (0.3.3) and chaoschain-sdk on PyPI (0.4.1) as of 2026-10-11.
Daydreams publishes @lucid-agents/identity on npm at version 5.0.0 as of 2026-10-11.
The Graph says the Agent0 SDK was built by Marco De Rossi with Consensys, MetaMask and Agent0 Inc.
Trustless Agent Day took place on 2025-11-21 at La Rural in Buenos Aires during Devconnect.
Trustless Agent Day was hosted by the Ethereum Foundation, Coinbase, Google Cloud and MetaMask and curated by the ERC-8004 team and the x402 community.
ERC-8183 "Agentic Commerce" is Draft, created 2026-02-25, and recommends integrating ERC-8004 reputation and validation through hooks.
ERC-8126 "AI Agent Verification" has status Final, reached on 2026-06-02, and lists ERC-8004 in its requires line.
ERC-8122 "Minimal Agent Registry" is Draft, created 2025-12-17, and is a separate ERC-6909 registry for custom deployments, written as an alternative to ERC-8004's one singleton per chain.
ERC-8217 "Agent NFT Identity Bindings" is Draft, created 2026-04-05, lists ERC-8004 in its requires line and binds an ERC-8004 agent to an external NFT through a metadata key.
ERC-8226 "Regulated Agent Mandate" is Draft, created 2026-04-12, by authors from Brickken.

ERC-8226 lets a verified principal delegate scoped, time-bounded and capped authority to an agent; it works with any agent identity system, gives ERC-8004 as an example, and says identity standards such as ERC-8004 offer discovery and trust signals but no mandate framework.
ERC-8004 has no protocol fee; users pay only gas.
QuickNode says registering costs dollars on Ethereum mainnet and pennies on Base, Mantle, BNB and Avalanche.
Cobo estimates registration at about $1 to $5 on Ethereum mainnet and about $0.20 on Layer 2 networks.
No published gas figure for giveFeedback was found in the ERC-8004 text, the contracts repository docs, the QuickNode and Cobo guides or a web search on 2026-10-18.

An eth_estimateGas measurement on 2026-10-11 gave about 155,185 to 178,504 gas for a first giveFeedback from a new client to an agent that already had clients (agentId 1); for an agent with no clients yet (agentId 0) it gave about 172,409 to 193,006.
An eth_estimateGas measurement on 2026-10-11 gave about 203,412 gas for register with a 67-character IPFS URI.
8004scan's statistics API (mainnet view) reported 699,098 registered agents and a daily new-agent figure of 21,477 on 2026-10-18; its home page had shown 561,576 or more on 2026-10-11.

8004scan's statistics API (mainnet view) reported 720,771 feedback entries and 755,027 users, which its home page labels unique wallets, on 2026-10-18; its home page had shown 682,170 or more and 496,805 or more on 2026-10-11.

On 2026-10-18 the 8004scan home page showed 29 networks, while its statistics API listed 31 mainnet chains (30 with a registry address; Plasma had none), including Solana, LUKSO, Shape, Gate Layer, Tempo and Arc, which the contracts README does not list, and not 0G, which it does.
The CSOAI census read 505,635 agent ids on Ethereum, Base and BSC, of which 358,401 were on BSC.
The CSOAI census counted 51,458 agent ids on Ethereum and 95,776 on Base.
The CSOAI census found 13,210 agent ids whose registration file declares an http(s) MCP, A2A or web endpoint, with 231,014 files not fetched.
The CSOAI census found 52,469 agent ids with no URI at all.
In the CSOAI census probes, 580 of 2,113 attempted MCP endpoints responded and 886 of 4,389 planned A2A card URLs served a card.
arXiv:2606.26028 found that only 3% (Ethereum), 4% (BSC) and 15% (Base) of agents exposed a valid registration file with a live endpoint, in data to 2026-05-13.
arXiv:2606.26028 found coordinated Sybil behavior among 73.5% (Ethereum), 59.2% (BSC) and 90.6% (Base) of reviewers.
arXiv:2606.26028 concludes that the Reputation Registry as deployed cannot function as a trust signal because values are not commensurable and feedback is rarely grounded.
arXiv:2606.12128 describes early ERC-8004 adoption as registration-heavy but operationally shallow.
Agent count is not agent quality: registry counts are token ids, not operators, and include placeholders.
A self-described agent account reported in a GitHub issue on 2026-04-02 that about 50 of 119,675 agents had sustained activity.
ERC-8004 links to x402 through the x402Support flag, agentWallet as payee address and proofOfPayment in feedback files, but neither protocol depends on the other.
The best-practices guide suggests that x402 facilitators publish cumulative revenues feedback because indexers cannot easily distinguish x402 payments from generic transfers.
Erik Reppel co-authors ERC-8004 and represents Coinbase on the x402 Technical Steering Committee.

The MPP payment discovery draft (draft-payment-discovery-01), whose four authors are from Tempo Labs and Merit Systems, cites ERC-8004 and says the discovery spec is off-chain but compatible with future on-chain anchoring.
Neither the Visa Trusted Agent Protocol repository (commit 16d59bd) nor the ERC-8004 text and contracts repository mentions the other (searched 2026-10-18).
Neither the Agentic Commerce Protocol repository (commit 7fdd78d) nor the ERC-8004 text and contracts repository mentions the other (searched 2026-10-18).

Neither the Universal Commerce Protocol repositories (ucp at commit ad9950b, with its samples, SDK, conformance and organization repositories) nor the ERC-8004 text and contracts repository mentions the other (searched 2026-10-18).

Neither the Mastercard developers agent toolkit (commit 2c6781c) and Verifiable Intent (commit 356c296) repositories nor the ERC-8004 text and contracts repository mentions the other (searched 2026-10-18).

The AP2 repository (commit e1ea56d) does not mention ERC-8004 (searched 2026-10-18); the link is indirect, because ERC-8004 lists A2A agent cards as services and AP2 can be implemented as an A2A extension.
ERC-8183 calls itself the Agentic Commerce Protocol, a name unrelated to the OpenAI and Stripe Agentic Commerce Protocol.
ERC-3643 is a Final Standards Track ERC created on 2021-07-09 that requires EIP-20 and EIP-173.
The ERC-3643 reference implementation lives at github.com/ERC-3643/ERC-3643, a GPL-3.0 fork of TokenySolutions/T-REX.
TokenySolutions/T-REX is archived, and its last push was on 2025-10-28.
T-REX release 4.1.6 was published on 2024-10-18, while the ERC-3643 organization repository marks 4.1.3 (2025-06-12) as its latest release.
ERC-734 and ERC-735 were never merged as EIP files; they exist only as ethereum/EIPs GitHub issues 734 and 735 by Fabian Vogelsteller.
ERC-725 has status Draft.
ONCHAINID key purposes are 1 MANAGEMENT, 2 ACTION, 3 CLAIM and 4 ENCRYPTION, and key types include 1 ECDSA and 2 RSA.

An ONCHAINID claim has the fields topic, scheme, issuer, signature, data and uri; addClaim accepts a key with purpose 3 (CLAIM) or purpose 1 (MANAGEMENT, which passes every purpose check), or the identity itself through execute.
The T-REX Identity Registry maps a wallet to an ONCHAINID and a country and exposes isVerified, which is a different thing from the ERC-8004 Identity Registry.
ERC-3643 is permissioned through issuer-attested claims, while ERC-8004 registration is permissionless.
In ERC-3643 an Agent is an operator role appointed by the token owner, not an AI agent.
ERC-3643 has no AI-agent identity, service endpoint or feedback concept (its Agent is an operator role), and ERC-8004 has no issuer-attested compliance claims or mandate model.
ERC-3643 is stewarded by the ERC3643 Association (ERC3643 ASBL) in Luxembourg.

No ERC3643 Association or Tokeny statement about ERC-8004 or agent identity standards was found on erc3643.org, in a search of tokeny.com or in a web search on 2026-10-18; a Tokeny post of May 2023 discusses AI agents and tokenization in general.
After feedbackAuth was removed, any address other than the owner and operators can rate any agent without proving an interaction.
EIP editor notes in the specification question the URIStorage dependency, the x402 example and the missing test cases.
ERC-8004 is listed on 25 mainnets in the contracts README while still Draft, and the Atlas must not call it Final.

A press release dated 2025-10-13 said the Ethereum Foundation dAI team and Consensys had launched a finalized version of ERC-8004, and the agenda for the 2025-10-22 community call speaks of a finalized spec, while the ERC was in Review; it has never been Final and returned to Draft on 2026-01-13.
The best-practices tradingYield example encodes -3.2% as 32, which conflicts with -32 in the specification.

On the default branch the README listed Polygon on 2026-02-02; Base, Monad and BSC on 2026-02-03; Scroll and Gnosis on 2026-02-04; Arbitrum, Celo and Taiko on 2026-02-05; Linea, MegaETH, Optimism and Avalanche on 2026-02-10; Abstract and Mantle (marked WIP) on 2026-02-12; and GOAT Network, Metis, SKALE Base, Soneium and XLayer on 2026-03-06, when the Mantle entry lost its WIP mark.

The Validation Registry reads are getValidationStatus(requestHash), getSummary(agentId, validatorAddresses, tag) returning count and averageResponse, getAgentValidations(agentId) and getValidatorRequests(validatorAddress).
In the reference implementation revokeFeedback reverts with "index must be > 0", "index out of bounds" or "Already revoked", and appendResponse reverts with "Empty URI" when responseURI is empty.

In the reference implementation giveFeedback reverts with "too many decimals" when valueDecimals exceeds 18, "value too large" beyond the value bound, and ERC721NonexistentToken for an unknown agentId.
The reference Validation Registry reverts with "bad validator", "exists", "Not authorized", "unknown", "not validator" or "resp>100".
The reference setAgentWallet tries ECDSA recovery first, which also covers EIP-7702 delegated accounts, and then the ERC-1271 isValidSignature check with magic value 0x1626ba7e.
The wallet-binding signature carries no nonce, so within its deadline the same signature can be submitted again for the same agentId, wallet and owner.
getSummary and readAllFeedback loop over every matching entry in the reference implementation, and the community audit in PR 51 lists unbounded array returns and quadratic gas among its findings.

The specification describes pluggable trust models tiered by value at risk, from low-stake tasks such as ordering pizza to high-stake ones such as medical diagnosis: reputation from client feedback, stake-secured re-execution, zkML proofs and TEE oracles.
The specification argues that MCP and A2A cover agent communication but not agent discovery and trust across organizations, which is the gap ERC-8004 addresses.
The specification enables simple filtering by reviewer and by tag on-chain and expects more complex reputation aggregation to happen off-chain.
readAllFeedback omits revoked feedback by default, and an empty clientAddresses list returns entries from all clients.
The contracts' upgrade notes advise operators to use a multisig or timelock in production and to consider transferring ownership to governance.
ERC-8126 was created on 2026-01-15, moved to Review on 2026-04-14 and to Last Call on 2026-05-12 before reaching Final on 2026-06-02.
ERC-3643 defines an Identity Registry (registerIdentity, isVerified), a Trusted Issuers Registry, a Claim Topics Registry and a Compliance contract whose canTransfer check runs on transfers.
In ONCHAINID a claim id is keccak256 of the issuer and topic, the issuer signs keccak256 of the identity address, topic and data, and third-party claims are checked with IClaimIssuer.isClaimValid.
T-REX contracts sit behind proxies that point to an implementation authority (TREXImplementationAuthority), and ONCHAINID identities support proxy deployment through initialize.

GitHub issue 734 (Key Manager) has status WIP and points to LSP6, issue 735 (Claim Holder) has status Discussion, both are closed, and the eips.ethereum.org page for EIP-734 returned 404 on 2026-10-11.

ERC-8226 requires EIP-165, EIP-712 and EIP-1271, defines IComplianceProvider and IAgentMandate, and assigns token compliance to a framework such as ERC-7943 or ERC-3643 and agent identity to a registry such as ERC-8004.
The ERC-3643 text is released under CC0, while its reference implementation is licensed GPL-3.0.

At Ethereum gas prices of about 0.067 to 0.097 gwei observed on 2026-10-11, 178,504 gas is about 0.000012 to 0.000017 ETH; later feedback from the same client costs less because it skips the client-list insert, and on Layer 2 networks the L1 data fee is extra.
QuickNode runs an ERC-8004 explorer at erc-8004.quicknode.com with a FAQ that says ERC-8004 has no protocol fee.
arXiv:2606.26028 reports that after removing Sybil feedback, 15.8% (Ethereum), 77.9% (BSC) and 86.8% (Base) of rated agents had no valid feedback left.
The contracts repository was created on 2025-10-08, made upgradeable on 2025-10-14, reached contract version 1.1.0 on 2025-11-12 and version 2.0.0 in January 2026.
The Review version of 2025-10-08 used a uint8 score from 0 to 100 and bytes32 tags.
Issue 99 of the contracts repository (2026-09-14) proposes grounding feedback in verifiable x402 payment proofs as a Sybil defense; it was open on 2026-10-11.
The CSOAI census also recorded 187,513 ids with no endpoint, 13,788 unreachable URIs, 2,205 invalid JSON files and 5,436 unsupported URI schemes, and labels its read state partial.
The CSOAI census dataset is licensed CC BY 4.0; it read the registry with eth_call only (no transaction or key), and fetched registration files and probed declared endpoints over HTTP.
The self-feedback check covers only the owner and approved operators, so a fresh address controlled by the owner can still rate the agent.
The registries never read the registration file, so an unreachable or malformed file does not fail on-chain; explorers and clients must handle it.

The 2026-01-25 update also barred the owner and operators from giving feedback, required a non-empty clientAddresses list in getSummary, added getAgentWallet and unsetAgentWallet, and typed metadata values as bytes.
A commit titled "mainnet deployment" landed in the contracts repository on 2026-01-31.
Operators are addresses the owner approves through ERC-721 approve or setApprovalForAll; they can set the URI, metadata and wallet and request validation like the owner.

On 2026-10-18 the Soneium Identity and Reputation proxies still returned getVersion 1.0.0 (the MinimalUUPSMainnet placeholder) and register reverted, while the other 24 mainnets in the README, Billions included (read through its explorer's public JSON-RPC endpoint), returned 2.0.0.

On BSC the Identity and Reputation proxies are owned by a Safe multisig contract and the Validation proxy by a separate EIP-7702 delegated account, unlike the single externally owned account on Ethereum and Base.

A deployed registration with a URI logs Transfer, MetadataUpdate (ERC-4906), Registered and then MetadataSet for agentWallet; setAgentURI also emits MetadataUpdate before URIUpdated. The specification lists the events without fixing their order.

The optional x402 identity extensions (sign-in-with-x, auth-hints and HTTP message signatures) identify the paying client, and the offer-and-receipt extension lets a server sign its offers and receipts with a key bound to its service; the core x402 messages carry the payee address but no statement about who the payee agent is.
